units_unreached.why: Not present in the node palette. I enumerated every palette category live (Target, Imaging, Science, Guiding, Mount, Dome, Flat Panel, Focus, Camera, Logic, Timing, Utilities = 36 items) and searched the palette for 'polar', 'align' and 'pole' with zero hits; confirmed at source: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/node_palette.dart has no PolarAlignmentNode entry, while the class exists (alignment_and_dome.dart:319) and has a full properties editor (_motion_rich.dart:966), summary, timing, validation and serialization. It is only reachable via Smart Night plan generation (smart_night_service/sequence_emitter.dart:242) or by importing a .json sequence.

Only surfaces in the palette when a plugin registers a node blueprint (node_palette.dart:510-571 builds 'Plugins / <category>' sections from pluginNodeBlueprintsProvider, whose default is an empty list). No plugins were installed in the scratch profile, so the palette had no Plugins section and the node could not be added.

findings.title: All 7 dome and cover-calibrator node types are dead: they always fail with 'No dome connected' even when the device is connected AND assigned to the saved profile
findings.what_happened: Ran a sequence of [Open Dome, Close Dome, Park Dome, Park Mount] with the Simulated Dome connected. Open Dome failed 6 times in a row with 'Open Dome failed: No dome connected', each retry logged '[RECOVERY] Open Dome promoted device disconnect to recovery', and the whole run aborted 2s in. The Equipment screen at the same moment showed 'DOME  Simulated Dome  Connected' and the header read '7 connected'. I then saved the dome into the active equipment profile (equipment_profiles.dome_id = 'sim_dome_1', verified by sqlite3) and re-ran: identical failure. Root cause at source: runtime_config_operations.dart:84-91 calls backend.sequencerSetDevices(cameraId, mountId, focuserId, filterwheelId, rotatorId) and there is no dome or cover-calibrator parameter anywhere in the contract (roles/sequencer_backend.dart:92-100). The Rust executor exposes set_dome()/set_cover_calibrator() (executor/setup.rs:149,155) but grep shows no caller outside tests, so ctx.dome_id / ctx.cover_calibrator_id are permanently None and instructions.rs:544,551 always return the failure. This kills OpenDome, CloseDome, ParkDome, OpenCover, CloseCover, CalibratorOn and CalibratorOff — 7 of the 37 node types — on every platform, with or without hardware.
findings.expected: With a connected (or profile-assigned) dome, Open Dome should command the dome. If no dome is available the app should say so before the run (preflight raised no equipment error for these nodes at all).
findings.repro: Equipment > Discovery > connect Simulated Dome (and Edit Profile > Add from connected > Save). Sequencer > Builder > add Open Dome + Close Dome > Start > Start Anyway.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-35-dome.png (Session Report: 'Open Dome: No dome connected' x6), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-36-domeconnected.png (Equipment: Simulated Dome Connected, '7 connected'), app.log 16:24:18 and 16:53:17 (second run, after profile save)
findings.proposed_fix: Add domeId, coverCalibratorId (and weather/safety/switch) to sequencerSetDevices across the backend roles + FFI, populate them from domeStateProvider/coverCalibratorStateProvider the same way rotatorId is, and call executor.set_dome()/set_cover_calibrator(). Until then, add a preflight ERROR when a sequence contains any dome/cover node.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live on my own profile. Connected Simulated Dome (app.log 17:28:55 'Simulator connected: id=sim_dome_1 type=Dome', Equipment header '4 connected'), added a single Open Dome node, Start Anyway. Log 17:30:33.680047 onward: 'Open Dome failed: No dome connected' x7 with '[RECOVERY] Open Dome promoted device disconnect to recovery' between each; run aborted ~1s in (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/verify-14-domefail.png). Source chain verified: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/backend/roles/sequencer_backend.dart:92 declares sequencerSetDevices with only camera/mount/focuser/filterwheel/rotator; runtime_config_operations.dart:84 passes exactly those five; native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/sequencer_api.rs:154 sequencer_set_devices likewise; grep across native/**/*.rs shows set_dome/set_cover_calibrator (executor/setup.rs:149,155) are DEFINED and never called outside tests, and node/context.rs:637-638 defaults both to None. So instructions.rs:540/551 dome_id()/cover_calibrator_id() can only ever return the failure. Profile assignment cannot help because no parameter exists. Two minor corrections to the write-up: (a) pre-flight is not silent — it emits an INFO 'Dome Operations Present — This sequence includes dome operations. Cannot verify dome connection at edit time' (verify-13-preflight.png); the finding's stronger phrasing 'raised no equipment error' is still accurate. (b) flat_wizard/panel.rs:94,151,211 also reads ctx.cover_calibrator_id, so the blast radius is wider than the 7 node types. P0 retained: it is a hard, permanent feature break on every platform, though it fails loudly rather than silently.

findings.title: 'Wait for Time' with no time picked returns Success instantly — a silent no-op with no validation warning
findings.what_happened: Added a Wait for Time node and left 'Wait Until' at its default empty state ('Select time...'). Pre-flight raised no issue for it. At runtime the log shows 'Executing child 3/3: Wait for Time' immediately followed by 'Child Wait for Time completed with status: Success' in the same millisecond (17:10:43.766494 -> 17:10:43.766505). No wait happened. Confirmed at source: rules/timing_rules.dart:17-18 does `if (waitUntil == null) continue;` so an unconfigured node produces no ValidationIssue at all.
findings.expected: Either a preflight ERROR ('Wait for Time has no time set') or a runtime failure. The single most common use of this node is 'wait until astronomical dark before imaging'; silently skipping it starts the run in daylight.
findings.repro: New sequence > add 'Wait for Time' > do not touch Wait Until > Start > Start Anyway. Node completes instantly.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-nodes/app.log 2026-08-01T17:10:43.766494 and .766505; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/props-waittime.png (empty 'Select time...')
findings.proposed_fix: Emit a ValidationSeverity.error when WaitTimeNode.waitUntil == null (and when a Loop's repeatUntil is null under the RepeatUntil condition), and make the runtime fail rather than succeed.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. Added a Wait for Time node, left Wait Until at 'Select time...' (node row honestly reads 'until (unset)'). Pre-flight (verify-43-pf2.png) listed only 'No Exposures' + a disk-space info — no issue for the unconfigured wait. Runtime, my app.log: 17:41:14.615986 '[PROGRESS_CB] Emitting NodeStarted: name=Wait for Time' -> 17:41:14.615998 'Child Wait for Time completed with status: Success'. 12 microseconds, no wait. Source confirms the named line: timing_rules.dart:17 `if (waitUntil == null) continue;`, and grep shows WaitTimeNode appears in exactly one file under providers/sequence/rules/, so no other rule covers it. Severity P1 stands — the canonical use is 'wait for astronomical dark', and skipping it starts the run in daylight.

findings.title: Run Script shows 'Timeout 300 s' but stores null, so the node refuses to run: 'Script timeout_secs is required in fail-closed mode'
findings.what_happened: Added a Run Script node, set only the Script Path to a working /tmp script, left the Timeout field showing 300 (rendered as a real value, not grey placeholder). Run failed at 16:28:21 with 'Run Script failed: Script timeout_secs is required in fail-closed mode' and the script never executed (target file absent). I then typed 60 into the same Timeout field and re-ran: the script executed and the node returned Success. So a Run Script node is unusable out of the box, and the panel states a timeout that is not stored. Three different numbers are shown for the same unset field on one screen: the editor prints `node.timeoutSecs ?? 300` (_misc_properties.dart:52), the Timing card right below it prints `${script.timeoutSecs ?? 30}s` (node_timing_section.dart:588), and the duration estimator uses `?? 60` (sequence_time_estimator.dart:189).
findings.expected: Either the editor writes its displayed default into the node on creation, or the field shows an empty/placeholder state and preflight errors on it. All three surfaces must agree.
findings.repro: New sequence > add Run Script > set Script Path only > Start > Start Anyway. Fails. Type any number into Timeout > re-run. Succeeds.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/cur.png at 12:27 (panel shows Timeout 300 and Timing 'Timeout 30s'); app.log 16:28:21.089822 (failure) and 16:29:14.398317 (Success after editing); /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-nodes/script-ran.txt only written on the second run
findings.proposed_fix: Give ScriptNode a non-null default timeoutSecs (300) in the constructor, or have the palette factory seed it. Delete the two divergent `?? 30` / `?? 60` fallbacks.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end to end. Added Run Script, set only Script Path to a working /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-nodes-verify/t.sh, left Timeout showing 300 (rendered in solid white, unlike the grey placeholders in Script Path and Arguments on the same panel — verify-68-scriptprops.png). Run: app.log 17:56:00.032158 'Running script: .../t.sh []' then 17:56:00.032225 ERROR 'Run Script failed: Script timeout_secs is required in fail-closed mode'; the script's sentinel file was never created. All three divergent surfaces verified simultaneously on one screen: editor field '300' (_misc_properties.dart:52 `node.timeoutSecs ?? 300`), Timing card 'Timeout 30s' (node_timing_section.dart:588 `?? 30`), pre-flight Simulation 'Duration 1m' (sequence_time_estimator.dart:189 `_defaultScriptTimeoutSecs = 60`, used at :597). Root cause verified: ScriptNode.timeoutSecs is `final int?` with no default (equipment_timing_and_automation.dart:531,543) and node_palette.dart:504 creates a bare `ScriptNode()`; instructions.rs:6329 returns the exact failure on None.

findings.title: Recovery node's properties panel says its trigger is 'Any Error' while pre-flight calls it unconfigured: 'It will never fire'
findings.what_happened: Added a Recovery node. Its properties panel shows Trigger Type = 'Any Error', Recovery Action = 'Retry Operation', Max Retries = 3 — reading exactly like a configured node. Pre-flight then blocks the run with an ERROR: 'Recovery Has No Trigger — Recovery node "Recovery" has no trigger configured. It will never fire.' Source confirms the contradiction: recovery_properties.dart:32 renders a null triggerType as the label 'Any Error', while logic_node_rules.dart:45 treats null as unconfigured.
findings.expected: The dropdown should show an explicit unset state (e.g. 'Select trigger…') or 'Any Error' should actually be persisted as a real trigger type.
findings.repro: New sequence > add Recovery > read Properties (Trigger Type: Any Error) > Start. Pre-flight: 'Recovery Has No Trigger'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/props-recovery.png (Trigger Type: Any Error); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-44-preflight3.png (Recovery Has No Trigger error)
findings.proposed_fix: Render null as a distinct 'Not set' entry, or persist TriggerType.anyError when the node is created from the palette.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. Adding a Recovery node from the palette produces a panel reading Trigger Type 'Any Error' / Recovery Action 'Retry Operation' / Max Retries 3 (verify-20-recprops.png), and the sequence error badge incremented from 2 to 3 at the same instant. Source matches verbatim: recovery_properties.dart:32 builds `NodeDropdown<TriggerType?>` with `items: const [null, ...TriggerType.values]` and `labelBuilder: (t) { if (t == null) return 'Any Error'; ... }`; logic_node_rules.dart:45 RecoveryNodeConfigRule emits ValidationSeverity.error 'Recovery Has No Trigger ... It will never fire.' when triggerType == null. Severity down-called from P1 to P2: the contradiction is real and confusing, but it is fail-loud (pre-flight blocks the run and names the node) and a single dropdown selection clears it — no data or night is lost.

findings.title: The Notification example template the UI itself suggests (${frame}) always fails and aborts the entire run, and the reason is thrown away
findings.what_happened: The Title field's own hint is `e.g. Frame ${frame} of ${target.name} done` (_capture_rich.dart:347). I used `AUDIT NOTIF ${frame}` as the title. At runtime: 'ERROR Notification title `AUDIT NOTIF ${frame}` failed interpolation: Variable `${frame}` cannot be resolved: frame number is only set inside an exposure burst' — the node returned Failure and the whole sequence aborted, so the Park Mount node after it never ran and the mount was left unparked and tracking. A Notification instruction can never be 'inside an exposure burst', so the suggested example is guaranteed to fail. Worse, the Session Report's Errors section said only 'Sequence failed' with no cause, and sequence_runs.stats_json recorded errorMessages:["Sequence failed"] — the specific interpolation error exists only in the log. (By contrast Open Cover / Open Dome / Start Guiding failures DO propagate their real text, so this is a Notification-specific loss.)
findings.expected: Either ${frame} resolves to something sane outside a burst, or the hint text does not advertise a variable this node cannot use. A template typo should not abort the run and strand the mount; and the run record should carry the real error text.
findings.repro: Add Notification, set Title to `AUDIT NOTIF ${frame}`, add Park Mount after it, Start. Run fails at the Notification; Park never runs.
findings.evidence: app.log 2026-08-01T16:19:34.199771; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-32-done.png (Session Report Errors = 'Sequence failed' only); sqlite3 sequence_runs id=1 stats_json errorMessages
findings.proposed_fix: Change the hint to variables valid in this scope; make interpolation failure a warning that sends the raw title rather than a run-aborting error; propagate the instruction's failure message into run stats like every other node does.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Every link verified. The hint is on screen verbatim: 'e.g. Frame ${frame} of ${target.name} done' (verify-74-3nodes.png; _capture_rich.dart:347). resolver.rs:258-262 resolves 'frame' from frame.frame with the message 'frame number is only set inside an exposure burst'. node/instructions/notification.rs:39-49 constructs `EvaluationFrame::empty()` — its own comment says frame fields are None here — and on interpolation error does a bare `return NodeStatus::Failure`, aborting the run. That bare early return is also exactly why the cause is lost: it bypasses `log_and_get_status_with_context("Notification", &ctx)` at the bottom of the same function, which is the call every other instruction uses to record its error text. Confirmed downstream in the prior run's DB: sequence_runs id=1 stats_json errorMessages == ["Sequence failed"] with no cause. P1 stands: a UI-suggested template guarantees an aborted run and strands whatever safing nodes follow it.

findings.title: Sequence header reports '0 frames / 0m' for a Science Photometry node that says '60 frames', and pre-flight claims 'No exposure nodes found'
findings.what_happened: New sequence containing exactly one Science Photometry node. Its own row reads '(no target) · L · 60 frames' and its properties read Exposure 2.0 s, Frame count 60 (=2 min of integration). The toolbar planning chip reads '0 frames  0m'. Pre-flight adds a warning 'No Exposures — No exposure nodes found. The sequence will run but capture no images.' Earlier, a kitchen-sink sequence with 2 Science Photometry nodes plus 30 normal exposures also reported exactly '30 frames'. So the sequence-level frame count and time estimate ignore SciencePhotometryNode entirely.
findings.expected: A photometry burst is the longest-running thing in a science sequence; the header must count its frames and its time, and the 'No Exposures' rule must not fire when a photometry node is present.
findings.repro: New sequence > add 'Science Photometry' > read the toolbar chip vs the node row.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-47-photometry-frames.png (node row: '60 frames'; toolbar: '0 frames 0m'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-48-photprops.png (Exposure 2.0 s, Frame count 60)
findings.proposed_fix: Include SciencePhotometryNode.count in the frame aggregate and its count x (exposure + download) in the duration aggregate; exclude it from the No-Exposures rule.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced for the frame count and the rule. A sequence containing exactly one Science Photometry node shows the node row '(no target) · Clear · 60 frames' while the toolbar chip reads '0 frames' (verify-16-photonly.png), and pre-flight raises 'No Exposures — No exposure nodes found. The sequence will run but capture no images.' (verify-18-photpreflight.png). Source: sequence_state.dart:170-178 `_countExposures` adds only ExposureNode and SmartExposureNode; exposure_rules.dart:150-156 NoExposuresRule tests only those two types. TWO CORRECTIONS: (1) the duration half of the claim is wrong — SequenceTimeEstimator DOES account for SciencePhotometryNode (sequence_time_estimator.dart:618-627, count*exposure + download overhead + one filter change), so the proposed fix's duration clause is already implemented; the stale estimator is the separate `Sequence.estimateIntegrationSecs` walk (sequence_state.dart:315, ExposureNode only). (2) I never saw '0m' anywhere — this build's toolbar chip renders only a frame count. Severity down-called to P2: planning numbers lie, but the run itself captures correctly.

findings.title: A deliberate Park Mount instruction trips the 'Mount Tracking Lost' trigger and pauses the run indefinitely
findings.what_happened: Ran [Park Mount, Change Filter, Autofocus]. Park Mount succeeded (Equipment later confirmed RA 00:00:00 Dec +90:00:00 Parked). 1 ms later the log shows 'Trigger fired: Mount Tracking Lost (mount_tracking_lost) - action: Pause' and at 16:31:59 'Paused: holding before the next unit of work in this instruction'. The run sat PAUSED with a Resume button until I stopped it 2m41s later; the Session Report says 'Recovery after recovery but tracking was not re-enabled on sim_mount_1: the mount is parked. Un-park it before resuming imaging.' The trigger has no idea a ParkNode intentionally stopped tracking.
findings.expected: An explicit Park instruction should suppress the tracking-lost trigger for the rest of the block (or until an Unpark). An end-of-night 'Park mount, warm camera, notify' tail is a completely normal sequence and it will hang on an unattended rig.
findings.repro: Sequence: Park Mount then any other instruction. Start. The run pauses immediately after the park.
findings.evidence: app.log 16:31:53.399218 (trigger fired) and 16:31:59.086646 (Paused); /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-38-af.png (PAUSED banner, Resume button)
findings.proposed_fix: Have ParkNode/ParkDomeNode set an 'intentionally parked' flag on the execution context that mutes the tracking-lost trigger until UnparkNode runs.
findings.verdict_reasoning: The headline consequence does not hold. I ran [Wait for Time, Park Mount, Change Filter, Autofocus] with the mount tracking beforehand. The trigger did fire spuriously (app.log 17:41:14.617479 'Mount tracking lost during sequence!' ... 'Trigger fired: Mount Tracking Lost - action: Pause'), but the very next lines are '[RECOVERY] Attempt 1/9 ... Loop succeeded after 1 attempt(s); resuming sequence' and 17:41:15.617019 'Mount tracking resumed, cancelling tracking limit wait'. The run continued and finished 'New Sequence - completed', wall clock 45s (verify-45-postrun.png). grep 'Paused' over my whole log returns zero pause events. I then re-read the reporter's own log: their pause at 16:31:59.086646 arrives 5.7 s AFTER the recovery loop had already resumed, immediately following the failed trigger-fired autofocus at 16:31:54.398981 — i.e. it is downstream of finding #8's mechanism, not of the park. So the causal chain in this finding is wrong and the 'hangs on an unattended rig' consequence did not reproduce. Residual real defect, worth P3: a deliberate ParkNode does raise mount_tracking_lost (triggers.rs:624 only checks mount_tracking_expected && mount_tracking_lost and has no notion of an intentional park), producing a scary run error 'Recovery after recovery but tracking was not re-enabled on sim_mount_1: the mount is parked' on a run that in fact succeeded.

findings.title: An Autofocus node placed after a Change Filter node fails with 'Autofocus is already running on this equipment host'
findings.what_happened: Sequence [Park Mount, Change Filter (L), Autofocus]. The Change Filter invalidated the AF state ('Autofocus invalidated: filter changed to L'), which fired the Filter Change + HFR Degradation triggers, and the trigger machinery started its own autofocus ('Executing autofocus as trigger recovery action') at the same moment the Autofocus instruction was running. The Session Report lists 'Autofocus is already running on this equipment host' as an error, 'Autofocus runs: 0', and the Autofocus child ended 'Cancelled'. Change-Filter-then-Autofocus is the single most common autofocus idiom.
findings.expected: The trigger-fired autofocus should be suppressed when an explicit Autofocus instruction is the next/current node, or the two should be serialised instead of colliding.
findings.repro: Sequence: Change Filter, then Autofocus. Start.
findings.evidence: app.log 16:31:53.498895 -> 16:31:54.398966; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/cur.png at 12:34 Session Report ('Autofocus is already running on this equipment host', Autofocus runs 0)
findings.proposed_fix: Take the autofocus lock in the trigger path with a try-acquire and skip (log) if an explicit AF node holds it, rather than failing.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Ran the exact idiom (Change Filter -> Autofocus, same sim rig, same 'Autofocus invalidated: filter changed to L'). The Autofocus node ran all 9 focus points and returned 'Child Autofocus completed with status: Success' (app.log 17:41:59.882955). No 'already running' error appeared. Source shows the fix is already in: instructions.rs:3515-3530 documents this exact race and provides `execute_autofocus_for_node`, which WAITS for the shared admission gate rather than failing, precisely because 'With plain fail-fast execute_autofocus the node then failed with "Autofocus is already running", which aborted the ENTIRE sequence'. The string at instructions.rs:3509 is only reachable from `execute_autofocus`, the trigger/one-shot path. In the reporter's run it was the TRIGGER's autofocus that lost the race and was logged; the node's 'Cancelled' status came from them pressing Stop on the paused run 2m41s later. Their supporting datum 'Autofocus runs: 0' is also not evidence — my run reported 'Autofocus runs: 0' in the Session Report while an autofocus had just completed successfully, so that counter is broken independently. Residual P3: the trigger's losing autofocus surfaces as a run-level error entry (log noise on an otherwise successful run).

findings.title: The Collapse button blanks the whole sequence tree to an empty grey rectangle
findings.what_happened: With a 4-node sequence (1 target + Slew + Smart Exposure) I clicked 'Collapse' in the sequence header. The entire tree canvas rendered as a solid light-grey block with nothing drawn in it — no collapsed rows, no target card, nothing — while the header still read '1 target · 4 nodes' and the button flipped to 'Expand'. Clicking Expand restored the tree correctly. The sequence is completely unusable while collapsed.
findings.expected: Collapse should show one collapsed row per top-level node.
findings.repro: Build any sequence with a Target node > click 'Collapse' in the sequence header > wait 3s > screenshot.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-41-collapse-grey.png (grey canvas, header 'Expand', '4 nodes'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-42-expand.png (restored)
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. With [Science Photometry, Recovery, Target(New Target), Slew to Target] (header '1 target · 5 nodes'), clicking Collapse in the sequence header replaces the tree content below the first row with a solid light-grey block containing nothing — the Recovery row and the whole Target card vanish (verify-24-collapse2.png). The button flips to 'Expand', the header still reads '5 nodes / 1 target', and clicking Expand restores everything correctly (verify-45-postrun.png shows the tree intact afterwards). One correction: rows above the collapsed region (the Sequence header row and the first top-level instruction) still render, so 'the entire tree canvas' overstates it slightly — but the collapsed view is still unusable, which is the point. Note the button is inert on a sequence with no Target node (first attempt with 2 flat nodes did nothing at all), so a Target is required to repro.

findings.title: Sequencer telemetry strip reported 'Mount: Tracking' for 2.5 minutes after the mount had been parked
findings.what_happened: Park Mount succeeded at 16:31:53 ('Parking mount sim_mount_1', status Success). At 16:34:00 the sequencer's telemetry strip still read 'Mount: Tracking' (green), while the Equipment screen at 16:35:31 read 'Parked' with Dec +90:00:00 and offered an Unpark button. Two surfaces of the same app disagreed about whether the mount was tracking, during a run.
findings.expected: The telemetry strip must reflect the same mount state as the Equipment card within a poll period.
findings.repro: Run a sequence whose first node is Park Mount, then look at the sequencer telemetry strip vs Equipment > Mount.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-38-af.png (strip: 'Mount: Tracking' at 12:34), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-39-equip-after.png (Equipment: Parked at 12:35)
findings.verdict_reasoning: I could not get the two surfaces into the claimed disagreeing state. At 13:47:08 the sequencer telemetry strip read 'Mount: Tracking' (verify-54-strip.png) — but when I checked the Equipment mount card seconds later it ALSO read 'Tracking' and offered a 'Park' button (verify-55-mountcard.png), i.e. the mount had been un-parked between my 13:43 observation ('Parked', Unpark offered) and 13:47, so the two surfaces agreed. I then parked the mount manually from Equipment (verified 'Parked' + 'Unpark'), but that immediately pushed the active run into a 'Recovering' state and the telemetry strip stops rendering when the run is not Running — so the comparison was no longer reachable. What blocked me: the strip only exists during an active run, and parking the mount during a run terminates the running state. Separately, the finding's reasoning is shaky even if the pixels are real: Equipment's 'Status' field shows PARK state while the strip shows the TRACKING flag, and the sim mount does report tracking=true while parked (the executor logs 'Setting tracking on for mount sim_mount_1' followed by 'Not re-enabling tracking ... the mount is parked'). So this may be a poor choice of what the strip displays rather than a stale poll. P3 at most.

findings.title: The daylight gate blocks light frames only when a Target node is present — a targetless Take Exposures wrote 3 daylight LIGHT frames
findings.what_happened: At 16:19 (Sun ~55 deg altitude) a sequence with no TargetHeader ran Take Exposures 3 x 2 s and wrote 3 IMAGETYP='Light' FITS files to disk with no gate at all. At 17:02, with the identical camera and sun position but the exposures under a TargetHeader, the runtime refused: 'Daylight gate: refusing light-frame exposure — Sun altitude 55.4 deg is above the maximum -12.0 deg for on-sky light imaging.' Slew is gated the same way. So forgetting to add a Target node silently removes the daylight protection for the exposures themselves.
findings.expected: The daylight gate should key off frame type (light), not off whether a target group happens to exist.
findings.repro: Sequence A: Take Exposures only (no Target) -> captures in daylight. Sequence B: Target > Smart Exposure -> refused by daylight gate.
findings.evidence: app.log 16:19:23/26/29 ('Exposure complete') + /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-nodes/captures/untargeted_nofilter_0001.fits (IMAGETYP='Light'); app.log 17:02:53.797955 (gate refusal)
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced decisively, and with the variable isolated better than the original report (same node type on both sides, not Take Exposures vs Smart Exposure). Site set to lat 40 / lon -105, Sun ~63 deg. Sequence A = a bare 'Take Exposures' (LIGHT, 60s) with no TargetHeader: app.log 17:47:01.815050 'Starting 60.0s exposure', 17:48:02 'Saving FITS image to .../untargeted_nofilter_0001.fits', three frames written to disk, no gate anywhere in the log. Sequence B = the SAME Take Exposures node nested under a TargetHeader: app.log 17:53:17.075500 'Daylight gate: refusing light-frame exposure — Sun altitude 62.8 deg is above the maximum -12.0 deg for on-sky light imaging.' and the run failed. So the gate is keyed off the presence of a target group, not off frame type. Severity up-called from P2 to P1: this is a safety gate that a user disables by forgetting an unrelated node, and there is no warning that protection is off.

findings.title: Captured FITS files carry no FILTER keyword even though the wheel position is known and recorded in the database
findings.what_happened: A 3-frame Take Exposures run with the Simulated Filter Wheel connected at slot R produced FITS headers containing SIMPLE/BITPIX/NAXIS/EXPTIME/DATE-OBS/IMAGETYP/GAIN/OFFSET/CCD-TEMP/XBINNING/YBINNING/SITELAT/SITELONG/FOCUSPOS/FOCTEMP/ROTATPOS/NS-SESID/NS-FIDX/NS-NPLN and nothing else — no FILTER, no OBJECT, no TELESCOP/INSTRUME, no RA/DEC. Meanwhile captured_images.filter for those exact rows says 'R'. The filenames are worse: 'untargeted_nofilter_0001.fits' says nofilter while the DB row says R, so the file name and the metadata contradict each other.
findings.expected: FILTER (and OBJECT/RA/DEC/INSTRUME) belong in every light frame; PixInsight/Siril/APP all key calibration off FILTER. The filename should use the same filter value the DB records.
findings.repro: Connect the sim camera + filter wheel, run Take Exposures, then dump the FITS header and compare with `select filter from captured_images`.
findings.evidence: FITS header dump of /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-nodes/captures/untargeted_nofilter_0001.fits (no FILTER card); sqlite3 captured_images row 1 filter='R'
findings.where: native/skotiq_native/sequencer (FITS header writer used by the exposure instruction)
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on a fresh capture of my own (not the reporter's file). /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-nodes-verify/captures/untargeted_nofilter_0001.fits header contains only SIMPLE/BITPIX/NAXIS/NAXIS1/NAXIS2/BZERO/BSCALE/EXPTIME/DATE-OBS/IMAGETYP/GAIN/OFFSET/CCD-TEMP/XBINNING/YBINNING/SITELAT/SITELONG/FOCUSPOS/FOCTEMP/NS-SESID/NS-FIDX/NS-NPLN/END — no FILTER, no OBJECT, no RA/DEC, no TELESCOP/INSTRUME. At the same time sqlite3 captured_images row 1 has filter='L' and the file is named 'untargeted_nofilter_0001.fits', and the Session Report's Targets table lists the filter as 'L'. So filename, FITS header and database disagree three ways about the same frame. The log line 'Saving rich-header FITS file to: ...' makes the omission worse, since the writer believes it is emitting a rich header.

findings.title: Every node failure is listed twice in the Session Report and raised as two identical toasts
findings.what_happened: A single Open Cover node failed once; the Session Report Errors section listed 'Open Cover: No cover calibrator (flat panel) connected' twice and two identical Critical toasts appeared. Same with the single Start Guiding node ('Start Guiding: Failed to start guiding: No active guider configured' listed twice). The Open Dome run listed the same string 6 times because each internal retry was recorded as a separate error, so the report's error count never matches the number of failed nodes.
findings.expected: One error entry per failed node (retries collapsed into 'failed after N attempts').
findings.repro: Run a sequence containing exactly one Open Cover node with no cover calibrator connected; read the Session Report.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-34-cover-result.png (2 identical lines), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-46-final.png (2 identical lines), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-35-dome.png (6 identical lines)
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced three independent times on three different node types in my own session. (1) Open Dome: one failed node, Session Report Errors listed 'Open Dome: No dome connected' SEVEN times (verify-14-domefail.png) plus stacked Critical toasts. (2) Daylight gate: one failed exposure node, two identical 'Exposure: Daylight gate: refusing light-frame exposure...' lines and two identical Critical toasts (verify-66-state.png). (3) Run Script: one failed node, two identical 'Run Script: Script timeout_secs is required in fail-closed mode' lines and two identical Critical toasts (verify-70-scriptdone.png). The error count therefore never matches the number of failed nodes, and retries inflate it further.

findings.title: Change Filter to a name the wheel does not have reports Success, and the Equipment screen then claims the wheel is on that filter
findings.what_happened: With no filter list in the profile, a new Change Filter node defaults to the literal string 'L'. The Simulated Filter Wheel was showing 'R' at position #2. The node ran, logged 'Changing filter to: L (timeout: 120s)' and reported Success; afterwards the Equipment > Filter Wheel card read 'L' at Position #1 — i.e. the UI now asserts the wheel is on a filter named L that does not exist in the wheel's own slot names. The Session Report did carry an honest warning ('Active profile has no filter list configured; node will use filter name "L" literally'), but the node still succeeded and the equipment display was rewritten from the command rather than from the device.
findings.expected: Changing to an unknown filter should fail (or the wheel display should keep showing the device's real slot name). The palette should not seed a fabricated 'L' when the profile has no filters.
findings.repro: Do not configure profile filters. Add Change Filter (defaults to L). Run. Compare Equipment > Filter Wheel before/after.
findings.evidence: app.log 16:31:53.398035 + 'Child Change Filter completed with status: Success'; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-39-equip-after.png (Filter 'L', Position #1)
findings.verdict_reasoning: The premise is false. I opened the Simulated Filter Wheel's own slot dropdown on the Equipment card: its slot names are L, R, G, B, Ha, OIII, SII (verify-47-filters.png). 'L' IS a real filter on this wheel, at position #1. The wheel was on R (#2) before the run (verify-41-equip2.png) and on L (#1) after (verify-46-equip3.png) — the node correctly commanded a real slot change and the Equipment display is reporting the device truthfully, not 'rewritten from the command'. So neither 'a filter name the wheel does not have' nor 'the UI now asserts something false' holds. The only true residue is cosmetic/P4: node_palette.dart:169 seeds `FilterChangeNode(filterName: effectiveFilter ?? 'L')` when the profile has no filter list, and the app already surfaces that honestly as a run warning ('Active profile has no filter list configured; node will use filter name "L" literally'), which the finding itself quotes.

findings.title: Three different duration estimates for the same sequence are shown at once (toolbar 0m, tree ~15s, pre-flight 1m)
findings.what_happened: Sequence [Unpark, Move Rotator, Take Exposures 3x2s, Delay 5s, Notification, Park Mount]. The toolbar chip read '3 frames · 0m'. The tree row under the header read '~15s'. Pre-flight's Simulation card read 'Duration 1m'. The run actually took 14 s wall clock but only because it aborted early; the honest full estimate is ~87 s. Also 'Segments 5' for a 6-step sequence.
findings.expected: One estimator, one number, shown consistently.
findings.repro: Build that sequence and read the three numbers on the same screen.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-30-preflight.png (Duration 1m / Segments 5, tree '~15s', toolbar '0m')
findings.verdict_reasoning: The specific claim did not reproduce and two of its three supporting numbers are misread. (a) This build's sequencer toolbar chip renders only a frame count ('0 frames' / '10 frames') — there is no duration chip there in any of my ~20 builder screenshots, so 'toolbar 0m' has no surface. (b) Tree vs pre-flight: for a 10x60s targeted sequence the tree row read '~10m 30s' and pre-flight read 'Duration 10m' — a whole-minute display rounding, not a divergent estimate. (c) 'Segments 5 for a 6-step sequence' is not an off-by-one: I saw 'Segments 2' for a 3-step sequence, so Segments counts transitions between steps, consistently. Genuine estimator divergence does exist in this codebase, but every instance I could actually reproduce is already reported elsewhere: the 300/30s/60s ScriptNode split is finding #3, and the SciencePhotometry frame/integration gap between `Sequence._countExposures` / `estimateIntegrationSecs` and `SequenceTimeEstimator` is finding #6. As a standalone item this is a duplicate with unreproducible specifics.

findings.title: Pre-flight warns 'Slew to Target scheduled at 12:47 before target rises at 03:41'
findings.what_happened: With a target at RA 6h30m Dec +40 (currently at altitude 89.3 deg, transiting in 6 minutes) pre-flight emitted two warnings: 'New Target: "Slew to Target" scheduled at 12:47 before target rises at 03:41' and the same for Smart Exposure at 12:48. 12:47 is nine hours AFTER 03:41, and the target is at the zenith. The comparison is clearly done on clock time without a date, so any target that rose earlier the same day is reported as not yet risen.
findings.expected: Either no warning (the target is up) or a warning that names the correct night and the correct rise time.
findings.repro: Add a Target with RA 6.5 h / Dec 40 at site lat 40, add Slew to Target, press Start around local noon.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-40-fwerror.png (both warning lines)
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim with the same coordinates. Site lat 40 / lon -105, target RA 6h30m00s Dec +40 00' 00". The target card itself computes Alt 77.8 deg, Airmass 1.02, Rise 03:41, Transit 12:48, Set 21:47 — i.e. the target is high in the sky right now. Pre-flight nonetheless warned: 'New Target: "Take Exposures" scheduled at 13:52 before target rises at 03:41' (verify-65-pf4.png). 13:52 is ten hours AFTER 03:41 on the same day, and the app's own altitude curve on the same screen contradicts the warning. The comparison is clock-time-only with no date, exactly as claimed.

findings.title: Pre-flight error title 'No filter wheel for SmartExposure' is untrue — a filter wheel is connected; the body says the real cause
findings.what_happened: With the Simulated Filter Wheel connected and green on the Equipment screen, pre-flight blocked the run with an ERROR headed 'No filter wheel for SmartExposure'. The body reads correctly: 'requires a filter wheel, but the active equipment profile has no filters configured.' A user reads the heading, goes to Equipment, sees the wheel connected, and concludes the app is broken.
findings.expected: Title should be 'No filters configured for SmartExposure'.
findings.repro: Connect the sim filter wheel, do not add filters to the profile, add a Smart Exposure node, press Start.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-40-fwerror.png
findings.verdict_reasoning: Verified at the named source. packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/sequence/rules/smart_exposure_rules.dart:174 sets `title: 'No filter wheel for SmartExposure'` while :176 sets the description to 'Smart Exposure "${node.name}" requires a filter wheel, but the active equipment profile has no filters configured.' The title asserts a hardware fact the app can and does contradict on the Equipment screen (I had the Simulated Filter Wheel connected and green throughout this session), while the body states the actual, different cause (an empty profile filter list). The consequence follows directly: a user reads the heading, checks Equipment, sees a connected wheel, and concludes the validator is broken. Not driven live for this one item — the rule text is unambiguous and there is no runtime behaviour to observe. P3 is correct: pure wording.

findings.title: 'Add Filter Plan' in Smart Exposure adds a duplicate of the same filter, with different defaults from the row above it
findings.what_happened: The node's own subtitle is 'One row per filter'. Row 1 was seeded from the sequencer defaults (L, 3 x 2.0 s). Clicking '+ Add Filter Plan' produced a second row also set to L, with 10 x 60.0 s — neither a copy of the row above nor a value the user chose, and a duplicate of an existing filter, which the 'one row per filter' contract says is impossible. Nothing warns about the duplicate.
findings.expected: Pick the next unused filter from the profile, and copy count/duration/gain/offset/binning from the previous row (this is what NINA's Smart Exposure does). Block or warn on duplicate filters.
findings.repro: Configure profile filters, add Smart Exposure, click '+ Add Filter Plan'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/cur.png at 12:56 (row1 L 3x2.0, row2 L 10x60.0)

findings.title: Palette search ranks description matches above exact name matches: typing 'Dither' and pressing + adds Smart Exposure
findings.what_happened: The palette filters on name OR description and keeps the original category order. 'Smart Exposure' has the description 'One row per filter; handles rotation + dither', so searching 'Dither' lists Smart Exposure first and the actual Dither node second. Building a sequence by search-then-click-the-first-result silently gave me two Smart Exposure nodes and zero Dither nodes; I only noticed by reading the accessibility tree afterwards.
findings.expected: Exact/prefix name matches must sort above description matches.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Nodes > type 'Dither' in Search nodes. Smart Exposure is the first result.
findings.evidence: tree dump after adding by search showed 'Smart Exposure' twice and no Dither node; palette code confirms the ordering

findings.title: Stop Guiding fails the whole run when nothing is guiding
findings.what_happened: A sequence [Stop Guiding, Start Guiding] with no guider connected: 'Stop Guiding failed: Failed to stop guiding: No active guider configured' and the run aborted before Start Guiding ever ran. A Stop Guiding node is normally used in an end-of-night or pre-flip block where guiding may or may not be active.
findings.expected: Stopping something that is already stopped is a no-op success (this is what NINA and SGP do). Reserve failure for a guider that is connected and refuses to stop.
findings.repro: New sequence > Stop Guiding > Start.

findings.title: Selecting a node and pressing Delete does nothing; deletion requires hovering the row and hitting a 3-state hover toolbar
findings.what_happened: I selected the Slew to Target node (its properties panel loaded, the row showed the selected outline) and pressed Delete. Nothing happened — the header still read '4 nodes'. Deletion only worked by hovering the row until an icon strip appears and clicking the trash icon, then confirming a dialog. There is a sequence_tree_shortcuts.dart in the codebase, so shortcuts exist for other actions.
findings.expected: Delete/Backspace on a selected node should delete it (with the same confirm dialog).
findings.repro: Select any node in the tree, press Delete.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/cur2.png sequence at 13:0x — node count unchanged after Delete; trash icon path worked

findings.title: Progress events keep advancing for a node that has already failed (Start Guiding reported 0->60% after returning Failure)
findings.what_happened: Start Guiding failed at 17:17:00.534353 ('No active guider configured') and returned Failure at .534366; the log then emits NodeProgress 0%, 20%, 40%, 60% for that same node id at .534424-.534521. On screen the node's bar animates forward while the run is already dead. Same pattern seen on Delay (100% emitted after the run aborted) and on the stale 'Slewing to Target 0%' panel that stayed on screen after a failed run.
findings.expected: No progress after a terminal result; clear the in-flight progress panels when a run ends.
findings.repro: Run a sequence with Start Guiding and no guider; watch the node's progress bar and the log.
findings.evidence: app.log 17:17:00.534353 vs .534424-.534521; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-42-expand.png (stale 'Slewing to Target 0%' after a failed run)
findings.where: native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/executor (progress callback ordering) and the run-dashboard progress panels
findings.verdict_reasoning: The evidence is misread. The cited lines are '[EVENT_SUB] NodeProgress received' — that is the Dart consumer LOGGING RECEIPT off an asynchronous event channel, not the native side emitting. Source shows the native ordering is correct: instructions.rs:4946 cb(0.0), :4954 cb(20.0), :4982 cb(40.0), :4986 cb(60.0) all execute BEFORE the `ctx.device_ops.guider_start(...)` call at :4990 whose Err arm produces the failure; nothing is emitted after the terminal result. The same receipt lag is visible everywhere in my own logs (e.g. 'Changing filter to: L' at 17:41:14.616062 with its 0% receipt at .616089, and a Filter 100% receipt at 17:41:14.717950 logged after the Autofocus node had already started). The whole cited window is 0.2 ms, so no bar can visibly 'animate forward'. The second, separate symptom in the write-up — a stale 'Slewing to Target 0%' panel left on screen after a failed run — may well be real, but it is a different defect and is not supported by the log evidence offered; it needs its own repro.

findings.title: Calibrator On hardcodes a 0-255 brightness scale and states it as fact
findings.what_happened: The Calibrator On properties show a slider fixed to 0-255 with the caption '0 = off, 255 = maximum brightness'. ASCOM/Alpaca cover calibrators report their own MaxBrightness (commonly 100, 1023 or 65535); the node has no way to read it and the caption asserts a value that will be wrong for most panels. (The node itself is also unreachable at runtime — see the dome/cover finding.)
findings.expected: Read MaxBrightness from the connected calibrator and scale the slider and caption to it; if none is connected, say the range is the device's.
findings.repro: Add Calibrator On > read Properties.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/props-calibratoron.png

findings.title: Smart Exposure claims 'Round-robin: RGRGRG…' regardless of what filters the node actually contains
findings.what_happened: With a single filter plan (L), the Rotate Filters switch's caption reads 'Round-robin: RGRGRG...' — naming R and G filters that are not in the node and describing a rotation that cannot happen with one row. It reads as a description of this node's behaviour rather than a generic illustration.
findings.expected: Build the preview string from the node's own plans, e.g. 'L L L' for one row or 'L G L G L' for the configured rows.
findings.repro: Add Smart Exposure with one filter plan > scroll Properties to Rotate Filters.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/cur2.png at 12:5x (single L row, caption 'Round-robin: RGRGRG...')

findings.title: Target node has two different name fields ('Name' and 'Target Name') that disagree by default
findings.what_happened: A freshly added Target node shows 'Name: Target' at the top of the properties panel and 'Target Settings > Target Name: New Target' below it. The tree row and every run log use 'New Target'; the node label uses 'Target'. Nothing on screen explains which one matters.
findings.expected: One field. If a node-label vs astronomical-target distinction is really needed, label them 'Step label' and 'Target', and default them to the same value.
findings.repro: Sequencer > add Target > read Properties.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/cur.png at 11:48 (Name 'Target' / Target Name 'New Target')

findings.title: Pre-flight never checks whether the devices a sequence's nodes need are present
findings.what_happened: A sequence of [Open Cover, Calibrator On] with zero cover calibrators discovered passed pre-flight as 'Ready with Warnings' — the only warning was 'No Exposures'. The run then aborted 1 s in on 'No cover calibrator (flat panel) connected'. The same held for the dome nodes. Pre-flight does check filters for Smart Exposure and structure for Target Scheduler, so the device-requirement check simply does not cover the dome/cover family.
findings.expected: Pre-flight should map each node type to the device it needs and error when that device is absent — that is the whole point of running it before dark.
findings.repro: Add Open Cover + Calibrator On with no cover calibrator connected > Start.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-33-cover-preflight.png ('Ready with Warnings', 2 warnings, no equipment error) then /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-34-cover-result.png (immediate failure)

findings.title: Settings > Files & Storage > Image output: after choosing a folder the field still says 'Not set' and the browse button spins forever until the app is restarted
findings.what_happened: Clicked the folder icon for 'Image output', navigated to /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-nodes/captures in the GTK chooser and clicked Select. The dialog closed, but the row kept reading 'Image output / Not configured / Not set' and the browse button showed a spinner. Navigating to another settings page and back did not clear it; the browse button no longer opened a dialog at all (clicking it produced no new X window). The status bar still read 'No save path' 5 minutes later. Only after stopping and restarting the app did the path appear (status bar 'captures', app_settings.image_output_path set). Reported here because it directly gates every exposure node: with no save path the executor logs 'No save path configured - images will NOT be saved to disk!'.
findings.expected: The field and the status bar update as soon as the picker returns, and the browse button becomes usable again.
findings.repro: Settings > Files & Storage > Image output > folder icon > pick a directory > Select. Field stays 'Not set', button spins.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/cur2.png at 12:07 and 12:08 (still 'Not set' + spinner), sqlite3 app_settings image_output_path empty at that time and populated after restart
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/settings_widgets/settings_color_and_path_inputs.dart:180 (_browse never leaves _browsing=false because the getDirectoryPath future does not complete); packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/file_path_settings.dart:35
findings.verdict_reasoning: Did not reproduce, twice, including the exact stated repro. Attempt 1 (Image output): clicked the folder icon, navigated in the GTK chooser, committed — the row immediately re-rendered as 'Image output / /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-nodes-verify/captures', the browse button returned to a normal folder icon (no spinner), and the status bar changed from 'No save path' to 'captures' (verify-31-nav2.png). Attempt 2 (Sequences row, mouse-only, exactly as written: folder icon -> select a directory -> click the 'Select' button): the field updated instantly to '/tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-nodes-verify' with no spinner (verify-33-seqpath.png). sqlite3 app_settings at that moment already held image_output_path, default_image_directory and sequences_path — persisted before any restart. The named source also already guards against exactly this: settings_color_and_path_inputs.dart:163-190 carries a `_browseGeneration` counter, a `didUpdateWidget` hook that clears `_browsing` when the authorityKey changes, and a `finally { setState(() => _browsing = false); }`. Note the exposure path this claim 'gates' was demonstrably fine — later in the session light frames were written to that directory. If the reporter hit something real it was transient (most likely the GTK dialog still open or dismissed abnormally) and is not reproducible as described.

findings.title: The validation error/warning badges in the sequence header are not clickable
findings.what_happened: The sequence header shows chips like '9 errors / 5 warnings / 1 info'. Clicking the red error chip does nothing — no popover, no jump to the offending node, no panel. The only way to read the issues is to press Start and open the Pre-Flight dialog, which is a strange thing to have to do while editing.
findings.expected: Clicking a badge should open the issue list (the pre-flight content already exists) and clicking an issue should select the offending node.
findings.repro: Build a sequence with errors, click the red '1' chip next to the sequence name.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-nodes-21-validation.png (identical before/after the click)

verified_correct: ExposureNode end-to-end: 3 x 2s LIGHT frames were captured, written to /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-nodes/captures as real 4.15 MB FITS with correct EXPTIME=2.0, and registered as exactly 3 rows in captured_images with matching producing_node_id and producing_run_id. I attacked this by comparing the on-disk file count, the DB row count, the toolbar '3 frames' chip and the Session Report 'Frames accepted 3/3' — all four agreed.
RotatorNode really moves the rotator: with Target Angle set to 45 the run reported 100% and the next captured FITS header carries ROTATPOS = 45.0. I verified against the file, not the UI.

LoopNode fixed-count semantics: Loop x3 containing a 5 s Delay produced exactly three 'Delaying for 5.0 seconds' entries at 16:38:22, :27, :32 and finished at :38 — 15 s, matching the estimator's 'Contributes 33.3% of total'. I tried to break it by nesting a Parallel inside it; the reset-per-iteration logic held.

ParallelNode is genuinely concurrent: a Parallel containing two 5 s Delays started both at 16:41:43.4929 and completed the container at 16:41:48.5438 — 5.05 s, not 10 s. Repeated across 3 loop iterations with the same result.

ParkNode / UnparkNode actually drive the mount: after Park the Equipment card read 'Parked' with Dec +90:00:00 and offered Unpark; after Unpark it read 'Tracking' and the next run's Slew was attempted. Verified on the Equipment screen, not just the log.

CoolCameraNode / WarmCameraNode do real work: Cool to 15 C returned Success and the telemetry sensor temperature was ~14.4 C afterwards; Warm at 2 C/min then walked it back to 20 C over 2.5 minutes with monotonic progress (6.7% at 10 s ... 53% at 90 s), matching the configured rate. I checked the live Cam temperature in the telemetry strip rather than trusting the progress bar.
DelayNode waits the configured time (5.0 s configured, 5.05 s measured, progress 20/40/60/80/100%).

Failure reporting for missing devices is honest and specific for cover, dome, guider and script: 'No cover calibrator (flat panel) connected', 'No dome connected', 'No active guider configured', 'Script timeout_secs is required in fail-closed mode' all reach the Session Report verbatim (the Notification node is the exception, filed above). The daylight gate and meridian-flip altitude guard also state their numbers ('Sun altitude 54.7 deg is above the maximum -12.0 deg', 'altitude is -8.4 deg which is below the minimum 10.0 deg').

Every one of the 35 palette-reachable node types has a real, type-specific properties editor — none is a bare Name/Enabled stub. The five with genuinely no settings (Stop Guiding, Park, Unpark, Instruction Set, Close Cover) say so explicitly in an explanatory card instead of showing an empty panel. I captured all 35 panels to /tmp/ns-audit/shots/props-*.png.

Pre-flight validation content is high quality where it exists: 'Recovery node has no trigger configured. It will never fire.', 'Target Scheduler "Scheduler" contains a "MeridianFlip" child... the Rust executor will refuse to run an invalid tree.', 'Live Stacking is in this sequence but there are no Exposure or Smart Exposure nodes. The broadcast will arm but no frames will be stacked.' Each has a concrete resolution hint.

sequence_runs persistence is accurate: 14 runs were recorded with correct started_at/ended_at and the right terminal status (failed / completed / paused-stopped), and the full node tree is snapshotted into sequence_snapshot_json. I cross-checked run 1's snapshot against what I had built in the UI, field by field (durationSecs 2.0, count 3, targetAngle 45.0, seconds 5.0, the notification title string) and it matched exactly.
coverage_note: All 37 seq-node:* units are accounted for: 35 were added from the palette and had their settings UI inspected (screenshots at /tmp/ns-audit/shots/props-<type>.png), and 2 are unreachable from the UI (PolarAlignmentNode is absent from the palette entirely; PluginInstructionNode needs a loaded plugin). Of the 35, I executed 20 in real runs against connected simulators (camera, mount, focuser, filter wheel, rotator, dome, weather; no guider, no cover calibrator, no switch): TargetHeader, Exposure, FilterChange, SmartExposure, InstructionSet, StartGuiding, StopGuiding, Slew, Park, Unpark, OpenDome, OpenCover, Autofocus, CoolCamera, WarmCamera, Rotator, Loop, Parallel, WaitTime, Delay, Notification, Script. Runtime NOT exercised for 8 units even though they were added and configured: CenterNode (needs a plate solver and a dark sky), CloseDome/ParkDome/CloseCover/CalibratorOn/CalibratorOff (unreachable at runtime for the same root cause proven on OpenDome/OpenCover), DitherNode (the preceding StartGuiding failure aborts the run and there is no guider on this box), ConditionalNode, RecoveryNode, TargetSchedulerNode, LiveStackingNode, SciencePhotometryNode and MeridianFlipNode-as-a-node (each blocked before execution by a legitimate pre-flight ERROR I could not satisfy without a target designation / valid child tree / exposure node). Two environmental limits shaped this sweep and should be treated as gaps, not as passes: (1) everything ran in broad daylight, so the daylight gate refused every targeted light-frame capture and every slew — the SmartExposure filter-rotation order and the dither cadence were never observed on-sky; (2) the built-in Multi-Star guider could not connect (it needs a guide camera), so all three guiding nodes were only exercised on their failure paths. I did not rebuild anything; the pre-built release bundle was used throughout. Two harness notes for the next agent: `shot` now crops to the window and writes a .coords.json, so screenshot coordinates must go through `click-img`, not `click-xy`; and the New-sequence button's 'Discard unsaved changes?' dialog appears only sometimes, so a blind two-click 'new sequence' macro silently appends to the existing tree instead of replacing it.
